subject: Approximating multidimensional constructs into unidimensional ones

messages.author: 180d1f93b85d3ad5
messages.subject: Approximating multidimensional constructs into unidimensional ones
parts:
Hello again!

As I mentioned in another post, I am trying to develop a scale that measures "comfort".

Now, I know (because I developed the construct by using interviews) that the concept of "comfort" is comprised by more than one dimension. However, I am not interested in measuring developing said dimensions... I only want to get a measure of "comfort".

In that regard, is it possible to perform the following approximation?



That is,

  1. can I treat my data as "unidimensional"? I mean, all dimensions would be comming from the same "comfort" construct... so they should be correlated anyway.
  2. For analyzing dimensionality... Is it better to use CFA or the confirmatory IRT that Mirt presents?
Thanks very much again!

German

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Approximating multidimensional constructs into unidimensional ones
parts:
I think you want a bifactor model if you are really only interested in the general underlying construct while the specific factors are more nuisance dimensions that should be conditioned upon to remove residual covariation. See the bfactor() function for examples.

Phil
